rows.label: haiku-1
rows.qualitative: The candidate is strongest in section E and in the pivot design (exchanges, session-level pass, $0.002/session, cold-read target), where it matches the reference closely and stays grounded. It is much weaker in section A, omitting nearly all tool-level friction the reference captures (zsh `======`, transcript-parser rewrite, spine_entries patch and rubric sizing, Keychain/config-dir deviation, the chosen linux-ssh topic, the arm-B bar), and it never names the repo path. Section C is its biggest liability: several user attributions are invented or reversed (user 'cited' the repos convention, 'did mental math', 'invoked live data is sacred', 'understood TypeSafe immediately', 'accepted via follow-up' when no follow-up exists), and D introduces non-spec origins ('Pragmatism', 'Principle') and a fabricated security rationale. Net: decent structure and outcome fidelity, but recall of granular evidence is low and grounding in the user-model sections is unreliable.

rows.label: opus-2
rows.qualitative: The candidate is strong on the failure ledger (Section A) and decision table (Section D): it reproduces nearly every tool-level failure with exact error strings, IDs, token counts and dollar figures, and its D origins match the reference almost row-for-row, including the 41%/59% split, $0.002/session, and the marks-case reframing. Relative to the reference it is weaker on a handful of specifics — it omits that ~/repos did not exist on the Mac, the <a prior project>/2026-09-09 provenance of the headless recipe, the user's "free arithmetic before designing" rule, the concrete cell-isolation flags (Read/Glob/Grep, --strict-mcp-config, --max-turns 8), and the enumerated 3-step plan — and it undercounts tool calls (~30 vs ≈37). Grounding is high; the only distortions are presenting the ~/repos path as a KB fact (the KB says <user-repos-root>), asserting the headless recipe was "written on Windows" (unstated), and the tool-call count. Section B is slightly diluted by mixing "KB facts surfaced" into a corrections section, but no fabricated claims were found.

rows.label: qwen38-27b-8bit-think
rows.qualitative: The candidate is structurally clean — all five sections in order, every section-D item carrying an explicit origin label (often with a secondary origin), no stray commentary — and its coverage of the narrative arc (bug-vs-by-design correction, "your call" delegation, gated execution, the post-baseline pivot, exchanges vs turns, cold-read targeting, ground truth from the ledger) is strong. It is materially weaker on numbers and mid-session engineering detail: it drops the 55,155 cache tokens/$0.576 cold-cell anatomy, the 22,585-char ≤400-char rubric sizing and multi-file-bullet rule, the 41% never-distilled figure, ~$0.002/session, the ~10x projection cut, 11 transcripts, 114 files, 2 commits, the git-identity convention, the <a prior project> provenance of the headless recipe, and — notably — the disclosed ~/.claude-home `-r`/`--continue` trade-off and the transcript-parser iteration. Its grounding is mostly solid, but it invents two assistant errors that never happened (an assumption that config editing would fix home trust; a pre-baseline hypothesis that routing was the expensive step) and inverts two user-behavior readings, recasting the "is it installed / what does it do" questions and the "bug" framing as demonstrated expertise where the reference treats them as growth edges. Net: better than the reference on origin labelling discipline and failure-by-failure command detail, weaker on quantitative fidelity and honest characterization of user knowledge gaps.

rows.label: sonnet-1
rows.qualitative: The candidate is strong on sections B–E: it captures the pivot, the marks-case redirect, the exchanges/session-pass design, the ground-truth plan, and the open asks with correct origins, and its D section is well-labelled. It is materially weaker on section A grounding: it inverts the outcome of the binary search (crediting Python re.finditer with the confirming evidence when the string literals came from the first strings|grep and both Python passes were empty/garbled), fabricates a "user explicitly corrected task 2" framing that it then retracts in the same bullet, over-claims the cold cell cost relative to three warm cells, and wrongly asserts the user has deep familiarity with Jev primitives when the user asked what the skill does. Recall gaps cluster around fine-grained harness details (rubric ≤400 chars / 22.6k chars, spine_entries patch, arm-B bar, answers.file.choice verification, commit attribution, cell isolation flags, zsh ====== glitch, transcript-parser retry) and a few user-model growth edges.
